newsitem.title: ITALY: BNL says cant take control of BancoNapoli.
newsitem.headline: BNL says cant take control of BancoNapoli.

text.p: Banco Nazionale del Lavoro cannot become the main shareholder of Banco di Napoli, but insurer INA could, BNL chairman Mario Sarcinelli told reporters on Wednesday.
Six institutions have expressed an interest in the sale of a 60 percent stake in struggling Banco di Napoli which is on the block as part of a plan to salvage the loss-making bank.
INA and BNL presented a joint declaration of interest and were the only two institutions to publicly announce their move.
"We could not become the main shareholder in Banco di Napoli. That is a position reserved for INA," Sarincelli said at a book presentation.
And he said it was possible that other groups, including foreign institutions, might join the BNL-INA initiative.
"We are not excluding anyone," he said.

Sarincelli said that at present, there were no plans for shareswaps between INA or BNL. "At the moment there is just an agreement to put a bit of cash (into Banco di Napoli), on condition that the documents we will get to look at show that it is worth the effort," he said.

Companies which have expressed interest in the Banco di Napoli sale have the right to study information being prepared on the group by merchant bank N.M. Rothschild, which has been retained by the Treasury as an advisor to the sale.
Sarincelli said that if BNL and INA did end up taking a majority stake in Banco di Napoli it would create the largest banking-insurance alliance in Italy.

Newspapers reported at the weekend that state national insurance body INPs, which holds around 11 percent of BNL's capital, had decided to oppose any possible bid, but Sarincelli said this need not be a problem.
"We can decide this with the unanimous support of the board or else just with a majority," he said.
The Treasury holds a majority stake in BNL. It has also taken temporary control of Banco di Napoli.
Interested parties have until December 20 to make a full bid for the 60 percent Banco di Napoli stake. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
